name: Warm Brown
lede: Warm Brown is a saturated orange-brown from the xkcd color survey of 2010, built by stacking the modifier "warm" onto the base color [[brown]].

sections.title: A modifier, not a story
sections.body: The name follows the same grammar as other crowd-survey names in our data: "warm" plus the base word [[brown]], rather than a plant, mineral or place [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system's nearest block is strong brown, about five units from that block's center [1]. Its closest measured look-alike is [[windsor-tan|Windsor Tan]], read as lighter and more vivid, followed by [[saddle-brown|Saddle Brown]] and [[chocolate|Chocolate]], both duller [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. A 2010 crowd-survey name has no particular reason to match an older painter's palette, and our archive's early centuries are thin too, so the absence is unsurprising rather than conclusive [2]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 41, chroma 56 and hue 63 degrees, a saturated, red-leaning orange-brown [2].
